lessons.title: hablo — one form, two readings
lessons.gloss: I speak, and also I am speaking — the plain present has been doing two jobs since chapter sixteen, and nobody said so

segments.text: Somebody phones and asks what you are doing. Answer with comer, in the present, without using the -iendo form.
You said como. Now think about what that sentence actually claimed.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: it was doing both all along

segments.text: Como. — I eat. And also: I'm eating, right now, this minute.
One form, two readings. The durative one is the habit — I eat at eight. The actual one is this moment — I'm eating, don't ring back. English keeps two shapes; Spanish keeps one.
You have been using both since the very first verb, without anybody naming either.
Which raises the obvious question about the form you learned nineteen chapters ago. If como already means I'm eating, what is estoy comiendo for?
Insistence. The progressive is not the ordinary way to say what you are doing now — it is the way to say it when the now is the point.
— ¿Qué haces? — Como. (perfectly normal) — ¡Estoy comiendo! — I'm in the middle of eating, leave me alone.

So the progressive is optional where English's is compulsory. An English speaker reaches for estoy comiendo every time and sounds oddly emphatic; a Spanish speaker uses the plain present and saves the long form for when it means something.
This is worth more than it looks. It means you already had a complete present tense before that chapter, and the progressive was an addition rather than a repair.

segments.instruction: Como as an answer, then Estoy comiendo as a protest
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *Como* as an answer, then *Estoy comiendo* as a protest]

segments.prompt: Give the two English readings of Como.
acceptedResponses: i eat and i am eating

feedback.correct: Habit and this moment, one form.
feedback.incorrect: I eat, and I am eating.

segments.prompt: Somebody asks what you are doing. Which is the ordinary answer -- como, or estoy comiendo?

feedback.correct: The long form is for insisting.

segments.prompt: So what is estoy comiendo actually for?
acceptedResponses: insisting that it is happening now

feedback.correct: When the now is the point.
feedback.incorrect: Insisting -- when the now is the point.

segments.text: How many readings does the plain present carry? (Two — the habit and this moment.)
And is the progressive required for right now? (No. It is for insisting.)
